title: `TIME + duration` unsupported; DST gaps and invalid dates raise
verdict: raises where the reference refuses or computes
description: `time + duration` is refused (`SchemaError`, no supertype). `replace_time_zone` raises on a local time in a DST gap (`non_existent='null'` gives NULL). `str.to_date` raises on an invalid date such as 2024-02-30 and, with `strict=False`, gives NULL; it accepts `2024-2-3` for `%Y-%m-%d`.
reference: `TIME ± INTERVAL` is refused (`time_interval_months`); time zones are outside the model.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
